utterances.text: In paragraph 4, Mr. Trifko, did you say that the title of the faculty, that is the last line of paragraph 4, the word "Islamic theological faculty in all of Europe" should be added?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: Yes, that was my remark, that it was necessary to add after the word "Islamic" the theological -- so that we know that we're talking about the faculty of theology.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And in paragraph 5 did you point out that in line 7 of the English version and the sixth line of the B/C/S version instead of the word "to 2000" the word should be "until 1992," that would be the correct year; right?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: Yes, that was my correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now look at paragraph 17, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Line 1 in both the B/C/S and the English version you told us that it would be clearer if after the word "the beginning of April" the year "1992" was added?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: Yes. That is also what I wanted to add so that we would know which year that referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And so to finish with this we'll move on to paragraph 18, last line. Did you tell us that you believed that a clarification was necessary by adding the word "and secretary of the Executive Board of the SDS," adding the words "SDS" here?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: Yes, I asked for that to be added so that it would be clear exactly the secretary of what body that was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now that we have made these clarifications to your statement I would like to ask you this: Now after you have given the solemn declaration, would you give the same answers to the questions that were put to you then?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: Yes, I would stand by what I said to the General Mladic Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender the following exhibit and that is the statement bearing the 65 ter number 1D01652.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles, in your written response it says that you do not oppose admission of the statement, not statements.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. And it was reflective, I think, the language of the original motion. But we don't oppose either of the statements, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D1652 receives number D761, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence, while the original motion states -- refers to annex A and annex B and seeks leave to present the evidence not a statement. Please -- I'm looking at the clock, Mr. Stojanovic. It's time for a break. Witness, we'll take a break of 20 minutes and we would like to see you back at quarter past 12.00. You may follow the usher. Mr. Stojanovic, could you tell us how much time you think you would still need?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm going to read the summary and then after that I just have two very brief questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll take a break and we'll resume at quarter past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apologies for the late start. Mr. Stojanovic, you are about to start reading the summary. Well, I think it's better to wait for the witness to enter the courtroom. Although we don't need him for your reading the summary, but I think it's more convenient for him to be able to listen to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will take this moment to let you know that we have no objection to the redacted document 1D0450 -- excuse me, 1D04058a, the proposed redacted version of the Maksimovic statement. There is no objection

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the registrar is instructed to replace 1D4058 -- I'm afraid I -- yes with 1D4058a. And D686 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Stojanovic. Witness, Mr. Stojanovic will now read a summary of your evidence so that at least the public knows what is in your statement because later they'll be able to follow the questions put to you in relation to that statement. Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Witness Trifko Komad is a professor of sociology by training and until the outbreak of the war he lived and worked in Sarajevo occupying a number of jobs such as secretary of the motorists' association of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and from 1986 he was in the republic conference of the socialist alliance of BH dealing with affairs of national defence and religious issues. He talks about the gathering and association of Serbian intellectuals in the end of the 1980S and the emergence of the need for political organisation of the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina because it was clear by that time that the remaining two constituent peoples in BH had already through political parties SDA and HDZ developed their own method of political work in a multi-party setting. He got involved in organisational and technical work preparing the programme of the new party, and after the founding Assembly of the SDS in July 1990 he became a member of the Main Board and later of the Executive Council of the Main Board of the SDS, and thereby member of the Political Council of the SDS. And finally, secretary of the Executive Council of the Main Board of the SDS. He testifies to the interrelations within the SDS, the role of Radovan Karadzic in the political life of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the intentions and goals of the Serbian people in overcoming political and international tensions, as well as sectarian occurrences in the party, illustrating all this by comments on a number of intercepts involving Radovan Karadzic and himself. He emphasises his knowledge about documents containing Variants A and B relating to the organisation of authorities in municipalities throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina and the reasons for the establishment of Crisis Staffs in municipalities and their role and tasks. He got out of Sarajevo on 6 April 1992, leaving behind in the city his parents who met their end there as a result of mistreatment and persecution, whereas his sister remain a permanent invalid. Later on he assumes responsibilities to organise and escort the movement of humanitarian convoys towards the territory of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina until the end of 1992 when he began to work in the bureau of the RS government in Belgrade. In the supplement to his statement which he gave to the Defence team of General Mladic, he speaks in greater detail on the position of the Serbian people, the Serbian religious community, and the attempts to wipe out Serbian spiritual heritage in Bosnia-Herzegovina before the outbreak of the war. He has indirect knowledge about the state of interethnic relations in Foca before the war and states that he had had opportunity to meet with General Mladic several times and gain an impression on his positions and the position of the VRS with regard to the activity of paramilitary units. This is all, Your Honours. At this moment I should like to tender this statement but also the associated documents, and I believe we have an agreement with the Prosecution who have no objections. I would now take the liberty of reading out all these four exhibits as I tender them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which statement do you want to tender? I think you tendered two statements. They have both been admitted, so I'm wondering what remains as far as statements are concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the statement that is now marked D760 mentions in four paragraphs intercepts commented on by the witness, and I would be so free as to tender these intercepts as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's the only thing remaining from what I understand. These are associated exhibits. If you name them one by one -- no speaking aloud, no speaking aloud, Mr. Mladic. You know the rules. Let's try to -- I have the numbers here. The first one is RM 65 ter 1D04475. There are no objections. None of them, Ms. Bibles?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 1D4475 receives number D762, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 1D04476 receives number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D763, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives number D764, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives number D765, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D762 up to and including D765 are admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now call up in e-court D761, paragraph 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Komad, you say here that you had occasion to meet with General Mladic, and I would kindly ask you to tell the Court in greater detail to the best of your recollection when that was and when -- where did these meetings take place?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: The first time I met General Mladic was in Pale in May 1992, when General Mladic arrived by helicopter from Knin, I believe, or somewhere. He arrived at Pale and his helicopter landed near the resort called Kikinda where the Serbian leadership stayed at that time. This was, I believe, the first meeting of the republican leadership with General Mladic, and at that meeting they discussed the principles and the way the Serbian people would organise their defence. I was not the main person there. I was just attending and it was mainly General Mladic and Mr. Karadzic who spoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember your second meeting?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: It was in July 1993 when a group of Serbs from the United States arrived carrying humanitarian aid. They applied to the bureau in Belgrade where I was then working and I was that group's escort. We were supposed to turn over that humanitarian aid to the Main Staff at Han Pijesak, and the second part of the humanitarian aid was delivered to Pale to the political leadership. I was at that time one of the people who were responsible for delivering the aid. The weather was bad, if I remember well. General Mladic arrived from Mount Treskavica, again by helicopter, and we spent that day together with those people from the US. Most of them were representatives of the Serbian Orthodox church from Chicago. General Mladic wanted to receive those people, to thank them personally, and that's what he did. And my third meeting with him was in Belgrade. It was very brief. We saw each other only in passing. I was working at the bureau, he came upstairs, we just exchanged greetings and that was it. Those were all my encounters with General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember that meeting in Belgrade, when was it?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly. I can't remember the exact time. I would make a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And I will finish with one more question. Paragraph 9, if we could look at it. Mr. Komad, in this paragraph you discussed the attitude towards the Serbian Orthodox clergy, mentioning some examples. Could you please tell the Court if you heard any first-hand or indirect knowledge about what happened to Serbian Orthodox churches during those years in the territory controlled by the BH Federation?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: In my statement I focused quite a lot on the spiritual condition of the Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina before the war. I pointed out a number of facts that speak about the neglect of Serb religious communities and even attempts to wipe it out. I illustrated it with a number of facts in my written statement, but I would also like to add that this process of discrimination and these attempts to wipe out this community was described by Mr. Ala Ukovic [phoen] in his book "Spiritual Genocide." He relates precise information as to how it happened in Bosnia-Herzegovina. I will mention just a few. The fact is that the war continued this aggressive, discriminating treatment of Serb churches and the Serb religious community in Bosnia-Herzegovina. If I may only just say that according to information from that book, 170 churches and monasteries were destroyed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- also 116 were damaged --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If an expert has written on this in books, then the Defence has an opportunity to call such an expert, but we are interested in your personal knowledge not in what you read in books written by others. So we leave it to that. I didn't stop you right away because -- but it comes down to opinion and perhaps even expert evidence which is supposed not to be given by a witness of fact. Mr. Stojanovic, this was your last question? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I thank Mr. Komad and conclude. We turn him over to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Komad, you'll now be cross-examined by Ms. Bibles. You'll find her to your right. Ms. Bibles is counsel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'd like to start by clarifying where in your statements and where in the events you might have direct knowledge. I'd first like to look at D761, paragraphs 15 through 17, which discuss several things including Foca. My question for you, sir, is: Were you in Foca at all from April through December of 1992?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Do I understand correctly then that none of your evidence about Foca comes from your direct observation of the events in Foca themselves?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you. And you've testified, I believe, at temporary transcript 54 as well as in paragraph 20 of D761 about a meeting in Pale at the Hotel Kikinda. Were you present for all of the meeting?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: Not all of the meeting, no. Not all of the meeting, but for most of it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Were you there when Tintor was describing what should happen to mixed-marriage couples?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Turning now to your other statement, to D760 at paragraph 29. You indicate that you left Bosnia and Herzegovina in late 1992 or early 1993 for Belgrade. Could you be more specific as to your dates?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: I think it was January 1993, but if I just may say this: I would come and go. I would go to Belgrade and return to Pale. I wasn't -- either in Belgrade or in Pale on a permanent basis. I mean, you could say that I was moving back and forth. My task was to form a bureau in Belgrade, then I would return to Pale. It was difficult. The phone lines were not reliable, so I had to return to Pale for many of the things that I needed to do. So I don't know if I've been clear enough. I would go back and forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: That answers my question. Now, while you were in Belgrade for the years remaining in the war, which organs of the Serbian government did you work with?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: Mostly with the main leadership, practically with everybody but mostly with the organs of power from the Assembly, other organs, and better said that it was work with the civilian organs rather than the military organs.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now --

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: If you need me to clarify, I can do that. I dealt with humanitarian assistance, protection of refugees, the wounded. So there were contacts with the military organs regarding the care for the wounded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just to be clear, these were Serbian civilian organisations of Serbia, not of the RS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Republika Srpska and then sometimes with the organs of Serbia if needed, both of them, because that was the function of the bureau, to be a link in all the co-operation and the assistance that was required.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thanks. Madam Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And because it's not particularly clear, could you describe the name of the bureau that you worked for starting in 1993 throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: The name was the Bureau of Republika Srpska. It was an organ of Republika Srpska. In the beginning it was conceived in such a way and then later it would have the form of it being an organ, a bureau of the government of Republika Srpska. It exists today, but now it's called the Representative Offices of Republika Srpska. Sometime after the war it changed its name. During the war the name was the Bureau of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: All right. And when you needed to go, let's say, up the chain of command, did you report to or give requests to Momcilo Mandic?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: Momcilo was the director of the Bureau of Republika Srpska for a time -- actually, it was during the time that I was working there.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll shift topics now.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter 31576 on our screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, in your statement D760 in paragraph 30 you challenge some of the adjudicated facts before the Mladic court.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, although we discussed it before court and I believe there was an e-mail, we should clarify that in D760 in paragraph 30 where there is a reference to the adjudicated fact 1946, that's actually in the Karadzic case. The parallel adjudicated fact would be 79 in this case --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, well --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Ms. Bibles, I was --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- surprised that the Defence without any further explanation presents to us comments on adjudicated facts in another case which I'm not aware of. So I have not discussed the matter with my colleagues yet, but I thought let's just ignore it if this is the way in which it is presented. Mr. Stojanovic, I do not know what you expect the Chamber to do with adjudicated facts in another case and comment on it. We've got no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, according to what we did while preparing for the testimony of this witness, the adjudicated fact from the Karadzic case is identical to the adjudicated fact from this case number 79, 79 in our case. It's an identical passage. And we did inform the Trial Chamber and the Prosecutor about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When did you inform us about that? I may have missed it, in which case I'm -- oh, this morning. Let's have a look. Let me just have a look.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The Chamber staff received an e-mail this morning at 8.53 from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. If that -- I have not read that yet, but if that explains the matter. But it would be wise to refer to these matters in court, but I have to correct myself that you had not given notice, although very late and in a way which is not the most appropriate one. I leave it to that at this moment. Then could we have the text of the two adjudicated facts to see whether they are exactly the same or whether they are not exactly the same. Similar is not good enough, Mr. Stojanovic. Do you have the text of the -- could you read them, the two, into the transcript, the Karadzic one and then the Mladic one. Do you have them ?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Could you read to start with the Karadzic one, that we have it on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 21st of November, 1991, the Assembly of Bosnian Serbs proclaimed as part of the territory of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia all those municipalities or communities and settlements where the majority of registered citizens were of Serb ethnicity and they opted to remain in Yugoslavia. According to the comparison that we made, adjudicated fact number 79 in this case corresponds to the text that I have just read out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it literally the same or -- could you read out the text of adjudicated fact in this case 79.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note we do not have the original in English or B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, as you know, my knowledge of English is not sufficient for me to be able to read it, but this morning I asked my colleagues to make this comparison and they informed me that the text in English is identical.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. I'll check that myself at this moment and you may -- Ms. Bibles can continue meanwhile.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before she does, I think, Mr. Stojanovic, it would be very helpful where you have a number for an adjudicated fact in this trial and in another trial to rather use in the statement the adjudicated -- the number in this trial, then we wouldn't be having this whole discussion of comparing adjudicated facts. It would save us more time then if you could refer to the fact -- the adjudicated fact of this trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's number 79 in our case, as Mr. Stojanovic indicated earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The statement was from the Karadzic case and so we felt that in the technical sense this would be the best way to notify you of this matter, in view of the fact that the paragraphs are in the Karadzic statement, from the Karadzic case. I thank you for your understanding.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, we have heard the description of adjudicated fact 79 in this case. And in front of you, sir, on the screen is a decision taken the session of the Bosnian Serb Assembly on 21 November 1991, which states in its first paragraph: The territories of municipalities, local communities, and populated places in which more than 50 per cent of the Serbian electorate voted for the same joint state ... and then we see the last portion of that paragraph which says: " ... shall be considered the territory of the federal state of Yugoslavia." Now, sir, you've challenged this adjudicated fact in this trial, but I would point out to you that with some insignificant differences this decision is reflected accurately in the text of the adjudicated fact; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: Look, I wasn't part of the Assembly organs. I wasn't a deputy or held any other function in the municipal -- in the Assembly organs. Therefore, this decision by the Assembly is something that I was informed about. But I'm not sure what you are asking me.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it true that the adjudicated fact which we've heard read out is accurately reflected by the decision of the Bosnian Serb Assembly on the 21st of November, 1991; that's accurate, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: It is correct that this is the original text, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 31576.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31576 receives number P6901, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I should not have admitted it yet without it being assigned a number. P6901 is admitted. Witness, the issue is that the adjudicated fact says: This is what the Assembly proclaimed. Now, whether that was right or wrong is another matter, but you said that the adjudicated fact is wrong. The adjudicated fact simply said what the Assembly claimed. Therefore, in that respect, it seems to be a perfect adjudicated fact because it is literally the same as what the decision tells us. So that's not very smart to do it that way, but also not -- I do not understand, even with the explanation of Mr. Stojanovic, how we should understand this. Because Ms. Bibles has -- and you agree with her, that this is what the decision says. How could you then say that it's not what the Assembly claimed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where did I say that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In your statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In your statement. You say that the adjudicated fact is not correct, but let's have a look. It's the last paragraph in your Karadzic statement I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Paragraph 30, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 30, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In the second paragraph of paragraph 30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think that it would be fair to the witness to show him the paragraph from the Karadzic judgement so that he could look at that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's totally irrelevant to -- well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: There's no judgement yet, but I think you misspoke or the interpreters did misspeak. It should be D758 -- sorry, D760.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said at the last paragraph: "I can state the following: These adjudicated facts are incorrect ..." That's what you said. And the first one was just read to you, that is what the Assembly proclaimed. And your explanation is -- has got nothing to do with it being an accurate reflection of what the Assembly proclaimed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please the next page in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: There it is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not recall giving a statement that the adjudicated facts were incorrect. All I did was confirm in my statement that the local commune was the basic sociopolitical unit and that it was possible that the locally communes as basic sociopolitical units exist and that's part of what I said in the Karadzic case. I'm not sure that I said that the adjudicated fact is incorrect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you attested to this statement this very morning, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You were asked by Mr. Stojanovic whether you reviewed them and whether you would give the same answers and whether it was all accurate. When did you read it for the last time this statement.

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: This statement, I read it when came here to The Hague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, yes, and your statement clearly says what your testimony is, isn't it? Okay, but you attested to it this morning so if you don't remember then you must not perhaps have read it very carefully before entering this courtroom. We'll leave it to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But, Witness, do you see this text on the left-hand side of the screen in front of you. The long paragraph, the last paragraph on that page, first line. This is your statement in the Karadzic case.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And it says: "These adjudicated facts are incorrect." Am I right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it's written.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you attested to it this morning. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, I'd next like to shift attention towards D761 which is your Mladic statement in which in paragraph 19 you say with respect to convoys: "It would happen that local bosses would commandeer all or parts of the humanitarian aid for their own needs which was explained away by saying that the people and troops did not have enough for their own needs. The Serbs' political leadership analysed this and concluded that such vigilanteism could no longer be tolerated and instead they created an organisational structure which would allow convoys and humanitarian aid to pass through, and I was tasked by the political leadership with co-ordinating this for some time in 1992." On what date did you stop co-ordinating the humanitarian aid for the RS political leadership?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I didn't receive interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Neither did we.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the end of 1992 when I left for Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could have P6770 on our screens, please. This is under seal and should not be broadcast. But the body of the text itself is not protected so we may remain in open session for this.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, on your screen you'll see that this is an Official Note regarding the British humanitarian aid convoy from an organisation called the -- or Serious Road Trip, and it involves it being stopped at the Mostar check-point. At the top we see it's dated 20 October 1992. This Official Note is addressed to the Ilidza war department, national security service, Ministry of the Interior RS, and it explains that medical equipment was confiscated because the crew did not have the right documentation. In the third paragraph the author of the document states: "The instruments were confiscated and immediately handed over to the Zica hospital in Blazuj ..." He also states: "The instruments in question were ones that were vital to our hospital ..." Now, sir, under your watch over these convoys, was it the policy to take items from a convoy rather than sending the convoy and its property back?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: The policy was to escort the convoy to its destination, not to confiscate anything, to take it to the destination; specifically, I escorted a convoy that was going to Sarajevo and in Sarajevo I turned over the truck filled with goods intended for Sarajevo, the same in Gorazde when it was under the rule of Bosnia-Herzegovina authorities.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, you're certainly not talking about the convoy that is described in this document from the 20th of October, are you?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: He's talking about policy, not what happened on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: Yes, right.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: -- let's take a look at another document with respect to another convoy.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could have P6771 and again this is under seal and should not be broadcast, but the body, the text, is not sensitive so we can remain in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, as this document comes up you'll see that it is another Official Note regarding the same British humanitarian aid convoy from Serious Road Trip. This one, however, is dated 17 December 1992 and it's referring to events on the 16th of December, 1992. Again, we see that it's addressed to the Ilidza war department, and I will take you to the first paragraph of the first page about halfway down to the sentence beginning: "They brought in paperwork ..." "They brought in paperwork on the convoy which is in order and so received permission for the passage but that they were to leave behind one-third of the cargo at Ilidza which they consented to with great difficulty." So, sir, what we see in practice, at least in this instance, was that when the documents are in order the Republika Srpska would take a third of the items to allow the convoy to pass; correct?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: Well, I cannot say that it was policy. It wasn't policy. I don't know if there were cases like that. I told you what the position of the leadership was, to take goods to their destination. But I don't allow the possibility that things described by you happened because we were not able to control everything, even the means of communication we had at that time did not allow us to control everything.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: We can move this document from the screen now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And, sir, shifting directions or shifting topics again, in D760, your Karadzic statement, paragraph 9, you describe that you were a member of the SDS Main Board and Executive Board. Now, you were not elected to those positions; correct?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: Yes, I became secretary and I was also co-opted into the Main Board. When I was elected at the parliament the president, according to the statute, had the right to nominate some people, I don't know if it was seven or nine people, proposing them to become members of the Main Board. I was among those nominees. And as for the position of secretary, I was elected officially at the Executive Council following a competition for a publicly known vacancy.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, to make sure that we understand this correctly, is it true that you were selected directly into the Main Board and Executive Board by Radovan Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: To the Executive Council I was elected following a competition when I answered a vacancy announcement, and into the Main Board I was co-opted.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And that means selected by Radovan Karadzic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Shifting topics a little bit now going to D760, which is your Karadzic statement, in paragraph 19 you describe that relations between the central and local bodies of the SDS were rather complex and that at the local levels there was a lot of misconduct and animosity from Banja Luka into the Krajina towards Sarajevo and later Pale. In paragraph 21 you state that leaders from the Krajina, and you name some of them, were co-operative in the early stages but then began to have problems as early as July of 1991. I'd like to discuss this area with you right before the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could have the transcript of 65 ter 20251 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, you'll see that this is a transcript of a conversation that was intercepted between Karadzic and local party officials in Prijedor, especially Simo Miskovic and Srdo Srdic. An individual by the name of Radomir Neskovic also appears on the conversation. I would first like to ask about Neskovic, is he an individual from Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: He was --

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: But I have to clarify if you'll allow me, he was a member of the Executive Board together with me.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Based out of Sarajevo. All right. Sir, he appears on this conversation --

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: Right. I believe he was born somewhere near Pale.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could you please wait for the next question.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, in this conversation as you see it appears that Mr. Neskovic is in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could go to page 2 in the English but stay on page 1 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And, sir, directing your attention to the lower part of the first page in B/C/S, we see Neskovic describing a problem in Prijedor, essentially that local Assemblymen are claiming more seniority. Now moving to page 2 in the B/C/S and to the top of page 3 in the English, he states: "They do not recognise any authority here, especially if you mention Sarajevo." Is this an example of the kind of animosity that you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: Roughly speaking, yes. But if you allow me to explain why Neskovic is mentioned in Prijedor --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, that's fine. We'll get to that. Sir, following with the conversation, if you look at the transcript, you'll see that Karadzic replies with expletives and a short time on the same page later he says: "And please tell them this: Whoever won't adhere to the policies of the party and implement the policies of the party but adheres to their own private policies ..." and there's some other words "let them sign here, let them leave their place in the municipality and we will put new people there." Now, sir, isn't it true that when faced with those in the SDS who challenged his policies, Karadzic could and would make changes to the boards in the local levels; correct?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: I don't quite agree. Maybe looks like that from this dialogue, but in practice it was the Main Board and the organs of the party that decided. In practice it wasn't like that, but he did react like this in dialogues when he was angry.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I think we can finish this quickly before the break. Sir, if we turn to page 4 in the English and page 3 in the B/C/S, about halfway down, page 4 in the English, we see a person named Trifko tell Karadzic that a municipality seal was given to Neskovic. So you were present in the room with Karadzic when this conversation took place; right?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: I can't remember. I can't remember that detail.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Is that the kind of thing you would have been doing or checking on for being able to relay to Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: To check what? Excuse me. What was I supposed to check?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If a municipality seal had been given to someone from Sarajevo who had gone to another part of the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: We didn't have any seals of municipalities. We only had seals of the party.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Do you have any reason to doubt that this is you in the transcript?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: I said I can't remember that detail. I can only confirm that we did not have seals of municipalities. We only had a seal of the party.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Moving on. In this intercept at the bottom of page 12 in the English and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before we do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did the municipality not use the party seal for that municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The seal of the party for the party, yes, but municipal organs had municipal seals. And municipal agencies also had their own seals or stamps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Bibles was asking you about municipal seals and you said there were no municipal seals, and the question here that Karadzic is asking is whether this document that is being handed over to him bears the seal of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us understand each other. A municipality as a sociopolitical unit is separate from a political party, that is to say the SDS --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and in all its documents the municipality has its bodies and its seals. The party had its seal. And the municipal seal of the party has nothing to do with the seal of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I do understand that. And Mr. Karadzic is asking this person called Trifko here, we don't know whether it is you, whether this document that is being handed to him, which Trifko claims was given to Neskovic, whether it bears the municipal seal. Now, you've told us that the municipality has a seal and Karadzic wants to establish the authenticity of this document by referring to this municipal seal to see where it comes from. In any case the point is earlier you said there were no municipal seals, now you say there are. So which of the two is actually correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then I didn't understand you at first. It's true that the municipal organisation of the SDS may have a seal, but it was not a seal of the municipality. The municipality has its own seal, it's a sociopolitical community. Here we are talking about the political party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Madam Bibles was asking about the seal of the municipality not of the party.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But she also wasn't [Overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I confirm again, we did not have a municipal seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles, I'm looking at the clock.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I was overly optimistic about finishing this section. Perhaps this would be a good time to take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we'll take a break and we'll resume at 20 minutes to 2.00. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we are waiting for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom, Mr. Ivetic, you in your e-mail this morning you said that adjudicated fact 80 was denied. Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I can correct that. I believe it was reformulated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Reformulated --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Denied as formulated and then reformulated in Your Honour's first decision on adjudicated facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now then there's no misunderstanding about this matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And if I may --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: -- to save time, thank you, we could go to the bottom of page 12 in the English of this document and page 9 in the B/C/S -- or perhaps we can't. Never mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, we'll now move a little further in this conversation to page 12 in the English and page 9 in the B/C/S. And, sir, we see down at the bottom the page in the English, and I'm not sure frankly which portion of the page in English, where it's suggested to Karadzic that he should disband the board and appoint new people. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We did not receive interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: It doesn't appear the witness's microphone is on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then ... Yes, now it seems to be on. I see at least now the red light. Could you please repeat your --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the page that is in front of me in the language that I understand, there isn't my name indicating that I am communicating with anyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, that wasn't the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, you're not speaking here, we're not looking for your words. But if you look at the middle of the page I believe it's Srdjo is speaking and he's tell -- he suggests to Karadzic that he should disband the board and appoint I believe it's ten people.

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: Srdjo is speaking --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: You see that?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: I do, yes. I can see it now. I can see that it's Srdjo speaking. I first understood that it was me speaking. Srdjo was the official in Prijedor and he's suggesting to the president that a decision should be taken by the party board. This is just a suggestion that Srdjo makes in his conversation with Radovan Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, are you aware that on the very next day, on 11 September 1991, Simo Miskovic and Mr. Stakic are elected as president and vice-president of the SDS Assembly in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender 20251.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: We can tender the transcripts, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You just want to tender the transcripts, but then of course we have a surrogate sheet at this moment in e-court so that should be adapted first. And, Mr. Stojanovic, attention was just paid to the text, the words spoken, not to the intercept itself, the audio. Not having any objections means that you do not challenge the transcript presenting the words spoken in the intercept itself?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you already reserve a number for the transcript in both languages and that a decision on admission will be taken once the audio has been separated from it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Reserved number for document currently with 65 ter number 20251 receives number P6902, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes and that number is reserved once we have the material uploaded as they should be uploaded.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we could have 65 ter 7101 now.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And, sir, we'll briefly look at these. These are the minutes of the SDS Assembly meeting in Prijedor on 11 September 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And if we can actually go to the last page now which I believe is page 5 in the English -- excuse me, page 4 in the English and page 5 in the original.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, we see the newly elected Simo Miskovic address the Assembly. We also see an individual who I want to ask you about. It's described in the English transcript as Nesovic who is there from the Sarajevo SDS Executive Board. Would you agree that this would actually be Mr. Neskovic?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: Yes, Radomir Neskovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you. And, sir, you see the description saying that the work of the local boards is central to the whole structure of the party?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And you would agree that that was in fact the relationship between the local boards and the main party, that there was a relationship at that time?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: Other than the local boards there was also a Municipal Board. The Main Board in the republic -- at the level of the republic, then you also had lower organs, municipal boards and then the local boards. There was the Main Board of the party and the local boards and then in between those there were the municipal boards, specifically the municipal board of Prijedor, for example.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And, sir, you would agree that within the SDS these relationships followed sort of the hierarchy that you've described?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender 65 ter 7101.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 7101 receives number P6903, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to discuss further the relationship, given your statement, between the local individuals and Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter 20414, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, this is an intercepted conversation between Brdjanin and Karadzic from 30 October 1991. Sir, we see that Brdjanin phoned Karadzic to complain about a dance being held after a number of Krajina soldiers had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could have page 5 now in the English and page 4 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Just a clarification. On the record I see the date of 30th of October 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In the document it says 31st of October.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Oh, it does. I'm sorry, Your Honour. I am corrected. It would be -- this should be the 31st of October it appears.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you for the clarification.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: We see Karadzic's reaction to this, where he states: [As read] "Come on, man, do your job. Don't call me about every major problem" -- I'm sorry, "minor problem." That is a major misread. Returning to the quote. [As read] "I am not your nanny. You have power in your hands and you have presidents of municipalities through whom you can exercise this power until we achieve autonomy. So you cannot, you cannot call me about every detail. You should exercise power rigorously and to the fullest. Not a single bird should be allowed to fly over the Krajina, and there must not be a shortage of men from Krajina for the army. You must establish all that ..." Now, just above this section Brdjanin has said that someone asked him to call Karadzic about all this. When Karadzic demands to know who he says "Kupresanin." Who was Kupresanin?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: Kupresanin was also an activist in the Krajina. At the beginning he had formed an independent party. I cannot remember its name right now, but I know that with the forming of the SDS he joined the SDS. His party fused with the SDS so that there was a number of people in the Krajina who were responsible for that area, including Kupresanin.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: So can we agree that Kupresanin and Brdjanin both spoke together about an issue and then Karadzic was called about this issue? Can we agree with that basic structure of the situation?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: Well, I cannot confirm that. It's something that we can assume - I don't have reliable sources in order to confirm it. It could be a workable assumption but I cannot confirm it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, wouldn't you agree or would you agree that it's obvious from this and the other communications that the SDS central authorities provided guidance, direction, and approval to the ARK leadership?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: In the field, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I tender 65 ter 20414, and would be -- we'll create a 20414a which would just be the transcripts for this conversation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the and the number already reserved for it?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number reserved for document 20414a would be P6904, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we'll hear from you, Ms. Bibles. To be -- the witness answered the question, but where you said whether it appears from this conversation and I think other communications, I do not know exactly what other communications you had on your mind. Apparently the witness had but ...

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, and I'll clarify the record. I was referring to the previous conversation, the previous document that I've shown him during the course of his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then you should have been used the singular rather than the plural. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, in fact, you've previously testified that in addition to Brdjanin and Kupresanin, Predrag Radic and Radislav Vukic were others from the Krajina who regularly sought advice from Karadzic; correct?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: Yes, they were local leadership at the Banja Luka Krajina level and there was this communication. To tell the truth, I did say in my written statement that there was situations when certain groups or individuals behaved wilfully, not respecting the principles. And this was a result of the fact that these were the first multi-party activities in our country. So the direction was not quite clear, but there were also ambitions which pointed to a struggle for power. So these were the things that had an influence on some of these occurrences.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And am I to understand you that in the end, when it comes to the SDS central authority and local boards, that those issues or those occurrences were resolved?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: Most often they were resolved through dialogue when it was possible to do it like that, by considering instances when Neskovic went to Prijedor on behalf of the board or when individuals would go out into the field in order to co-ordinate these things and define the line which was laid down by the party. We always sought to resolve outstanding issues in a democratic way.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'd now like to change topics and shift attention towards your statement in D760, your Karadzic statement, paragraph 23, where you indicate that Variant A and B was something that JNA generals were working on but were not adopted. Sir, the Prosecution case is that these instructions were issued on 19 December 1991 by the SDS Main Board and they were commonly referred to as Variant A and B instructions. I'd like to just go through some examples with respect to how these instructions may have existed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: First if the Prosecution could have P3771.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, these are the minutes for the 6th meeting of the Executive Board in Kljuc held on the 23rd of December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: May I ask something? Am I permitted to put a question, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're not. If at the end of your statement you would like to add something which is important, then you have an opportunity to do so, but you should listen to questions and answer them -- unless it is a question of a practical kind such as: Could I have a hard copy of my statement or something like that, that's okay. But not about the substance of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir --

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: I actually wanted to ask which Executive Board? You said "Executive Board meeting." Which Executive Board? Whose Executive Board?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you. It's the 6th meeting of the executive committee of the SDS Municipal Board in Kljuc held on the 23rd of December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Now on page 1 in both versions, down where it says AD-1 it states: "Veljko Kondic informed the meeting of the instructions for the organisation and activities of the Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina. All organs will be required to work in accordance with the instructions. Whoever is not ready to fulfil his duties should say so immediately and it will not be held against him." And then if we go down further on the page in English and I believe it's on the next page in the original, right above the composition of the Crisis Staff, the document's reference is Kondic again as stating: "That means that all suggestions and tasks from the instructions are accepted in their entirety." They then go forward and set up a Crisis Staff and describe its membership. Sir, were you aware that the Kljuc SDS executive committee was acting on these 19 December 1991 instructions?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: We'll move on then to P3773.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, these are the minutes of a meeting of the Prijedor Municipal Board of the SDS on 27 December 1991. We see on page 1 in both versions under the title "proceedings" that Miskovic, president of the Prijedor SDS Municipal Board read out the instructions forwarded to the Prijedor SDS Municipal Board by the Assembly of the Serbian People of Bosnia-Herzegovina. It then states: "Since there were two versions, only version II which is relevant for Prijedor municipality was read out. "Having read out all of the items in sections A and B of version II, Miskovic explained what had been done so far with respect to the instructions." And, sir, if we look to the bottom in English - and I am not sure in the B/C/S I just realised - it appears on the same page, we see the words "reasons and functions were stated for the establishment of the municipal Crisis Staff and local staffs on territory of the municipality." Sir, as secretary of the Executive Board of the SDS, a member of the Main Board, were you aware that the Prijedor SDS Municipal Board was acting according to these instructions?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: No, because you can see in one paragraph it says that this is the Assembly of the Serbian people. The Assembly is a state organ, whereas I have a party function. I said in my statement that I never attended any sessions of organs that adopted these variants, and I also said that no organ reviewed or recorded or put on its agenda or protocol or put a seal or signed any of these variants. I don't know if the Assembly of the Serbian people adopted anything; that could have happened without my knowledge. Because you can see in item 1 of the agenda it says the Assembly of the Serbian People of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, in your statement you indicate that Variant A and B instructions never came to fruition. Having seen these documents, do you change your position on that? Do you believe that, in fact, the Variant A and B instructions came into being and were acted upon?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: I said in my statement that the organs of the Serbian Democratic Party, i.e., the Main Board, the Executive Board, the commissions and committees did not officially review this material. Had they been considering this material, this would be something that would be on record, it would be signed and recorded in the protocol. This is what I said in my statement which I signed and that I stand behind.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, if these were secret instructions at the time, wouldn't you agree that they would not have gone through the formal process that you describe?

utterances.speaker: TRIFKO KOMAD
utterances.text: It would have gone through the formal process but it would have been marked as confidential or secret. I did not deny hearing of it. As it says in my statements, I did hear that there was some talk about something like that, but I did also say that I did not attend any meetings where the party organs would be adopting something like that and I never heard of such a thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But, Witness, am I -- I'm slightly confused now. You said -- you earlier said: Well, this document says it is the Assembly of the Serbian People of Bosnia-Herzegovina. But the document itself is from the SDS, which is a party. And I think in your statement you said: None of the party bodies discussed or adopted this document. Now, there clearly seems to be a discussion or at least it's part of a meeting of the party, not -- this is not an assembly, a state organ, this is a party meeting. So I'm a bit confused about your explanation. Could you assist me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I reacted in relation to the document in front of me which states that in item 1 that the implementation of decisions and positions taken by the Assembly of the Serbian people of B&H. So that's what it says in the document. The Assembly of the Serbian people referred to in item 1. It says: "By the Assembly of the Serbian people ..." This is what my reaction was in relation to. I cannot discuss documents of the Assembly; I wasn't a member of it. But I said earlier and now that organs of the Serbian Democratic Party as a party never looked at these documents at any meetings that I'm aware of and I should be aware of all of them. I did hear rumours about this perhaps coming under consideration, but I did not ever take part in anything like that. I hope that I was clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you said that none of the party bodies discussed or adopted this document. Now, for the part of adopted I would agree with you that this document says that the instructions were forwarded to the SDS Municipal Board by the Assembly of the Serbian people of Bosnia and Herzegovina. But it's clear, isn't it, that during this meeting, which is a party meeting, because it reads at the top "Serbian Democratic Party of Bosnia and Herzegovina," and it's a meeting of that party where these instructions were introduced, explained, action was taken upon them. So that is slightly different from what you said: Well, we never discussed or adopted that. Would you agree that this is apparently a subject of what was discussed in this meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once again, I repeat that I stand by my previous statement, and if you have any evidence pointing in the direction of any organs of the SDS considering this issue, then please put it before me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the implementation seems to be part of what was discussed at this meeting. So to that extent I would say that evidence of that, understood in that way, is at this moment in front of you on your screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But it is not stated anywhere in this document that these were documents of the Serbian Democratic Party or showing that these documents, these texts, were adopted by any organs of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I leave it to that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I'm mindful of the clock.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you give us any idea as to how much time you would still need tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I anticipate needing about somewhere between 30 and 40 minutes. I'll finish in the first session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would then stay within the assessment of the time. Mr. Komad, we'll adjourn for the day. We would like to see you back tomorrow morning and we expect that your testimony will be concluded tomorrow morning. We would like to see you back at 9.30 in the morning in this same courtroom, but I first want to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone about your testimony, whether that is testimony you have given today or whether that is testimony which you will give tomorrow. So speak or communicate with no one about your testimony. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've been advised that 65 ter 20414a or P6904 is now in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and then, Madam Registrar, you certainly know what number had been reserved for that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It was number P6904 reserved for 20414a.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it now having been uploaded, P6904 is admitted into evidence. We adjourn for the day and we will resume tomorrow, Tuesday, the 11th of November, 9.30 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 11th day of November, 2014, at 9.30 a.m. 24 25
